headline: OpenAI's chief executive told Fortune he believes no lab has solved keeping AI in line with human values, but that OpenAI's current model is no existential threat.
score_reason: Pool score kept: on-record statements by the chief executive of a leading lab, matched to Fortune's own article; they are claims, not independent findings.
importance_line: People living alongside advanced AI, and lawmakers and investors weighing how fast it should advance, hear OpenAI's chief say making AI follow human values is unsolved, but these are one executive's statements, not an independent finding.
summary: Fortune reports, in an interview with OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman, that he said "We have not solved alignment", the problem of making AI act in line with human values, and that he believes no lab has, while stressing that OpenAI's current flagship model, Astra, is not an existential threat. Altman called a 10 percent chance of AI destroying humanity by the end of the decade unacceptable and said OpenAI would pause for safety even against its investors' financial interests, but he argued against stopping AI development altogether.
notes: Pool item is Livemint's summary of the Fortune interview; Fortune's own article (Alyson Shontell) was read, matches Livemint, and is credited and linked as the first reporter. Fortune also reports Altman saying OpenAI will not go public this year (not in Livemint); the entry leaves it out and C05-04's notes mention it.
